---
title: "Contribute a page"
---

The catalog lists **266 models**; no single group will build them all. Pages are
individually authored and individually credited, with your name and ORCID on the
page and in the release metadata.

## Pick a model

Browse [`models.yaml`](https://github.com/pymrm/pymrm-gallery/blob/main/models.yaml)
for entries with `status: planned`, or the full survey in
[`docs/`](https://github.com/pymrm/pymrm-gallery/tree/main/docs) for the ~236
catalogued models not yet migrated into the index. Open an issue to claim one so
two people do not build the same page.

**Published work only.** The gallery reproduces models that have appeared in the
literature. Entries whose source is still in preparation, under review, or in
revision carry `status: deferred` with a `blocked_by` note; please do not build
those, including your own. A gallery that reproduces the published literature is
weakened by pages nobody can check against a publication.

Good first pages have: a clear primary reference, data in a table or an open
repository rather than a figure, and structure `S1`–`S6`.

## Build it

```bash
git clone https://github.com/pymrm/pymrm-gallery && cd pymrm-gallery
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp -r templates/page-skeleton pages/<catalog-id>-<slug>
```

Fill in the nine required sections: *Background · The published model ·
Parameters and assumptions · The data · PyMRM implementation · Results ·
Validation · What pymrm adds · Reuse*.

Rules that CI enforces:

- **Cell 1 is the Colab environment cell.** The notebook must run on a fresh
  Colab VM with no repository checkout.
- **Load data through `gallery_utils.load_data`**, never a bare relative path.
- **Every CSV needs a `.meta.yaml` provenance sidecar.** Schema and legal basis:
  [`docs/data-strategy.md`](https://github.com/pymrm/pymrm-gallery/blob/main/docs/data-strategy.md).
- **No source PDFs, ever.** DOIs and extracted CSVs only.
- **No Quarto-only Markdown in `index.ipynb`** — no `:::` blocks, no shortcodes.
  The notebook must render in Jupyter, GitHub, and VS Code.
- **At least one validation** that does not use the experimental data.
- **Call `report_agreement(...)`** so metric regressions are caught.

Then:

```bash
python scripts/check_metadata.py
python scripts/run_pages.py
```

## Never fabricate data

If you cannot obtain the experimental data, build the page against an analytical
solution or a high-fidelity reference and **label it as such**, or leave the
dataset as a placeholder and mark the page `status: planned`. A page with
invented numbers is worse than no page, and it is the one thing that would
destroy the gallery's usefulness.

The same applies to the *What pymrm adds* section. If the page is a faithful
reproduction with no extension, write that.

## Review

A maintainer checks four things: the physics is right, the data provenance is
complete and honest, the notebook executes from a clean environment, and a
validation is present. This is a quality gate, not peer review — we are trying
to keep the barrier low.

## Using a coding agent

Encouraged. Point it at
[`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/pymrm/pymrm-gallery/blob/main/AGENTS.md), which
tells it to start from `models.yaml`, copy the structurally nearest existing
page, and follow the pymrm conventions. You remain responsible for the physics
and for the honesty of the data provenance — please check both before opening a
PR.
